Subject: Post-Landfall Directive – Shelter Management and Repatriation of Evacuees

The cyclone has made landfall and the wind speed has reduced considerably. However, the danger is not yet over. Heavy rain continues in several blocks and waterlogging is reported from low-lying areas. All Shelter Incharges and nodal officers shall continue to function until further orders. The following directions are issued for the management of shelters and the safe return of evacuees.

1.  No evacuee shall be permitted to leave the shelter until the DEOC issues an explicit "All Clear" message. The All Clear shall be communicated through the DEOC Control Room only, and not by any other authority. Shelters shall not act on verbal instructions or on the basis of weather reports received directly.

2.  Shelter Incharges shall prepare a list of evacuees shelter-wise, block-wise, and village-wise. The list shall show the number of families and persons still present in the shelter as on 15-07-2026 evening, and the number of families who have already returned to their villages on their own. This list shall be submitted to the DEOC Control Room by 20:00 Hrs. today.

3.  The transport arrangements made for evacuation shall be used in the reverse direction for repatriation. The vehicles shall be deployed only after the All Clear is given. The Shelter Incharge shall coordinate with the transport nodal officer for this purpose.

4.  The Shelter Incharges shall ensure that the shelters are cleaned before the evacuees are sent back. Drinking water and food arrangements shall continue until the last evacuee leaves the shelter. The health teams shall visit each shelter at least twice a day and report any case of illness to the DEOC Control Room.

5.  The DEOC Control Room shall maintain a register of all complaints received from evacuees regarding missing persons, lost belongings, or damage to houses. The register shall be handed over to the Revenue Department after the shelters are closed.

6.  The Shelter Incharges shall submit a daily report on the condition of the shelter building, including any damage to the roof, walls, or sanitary facilities. The report shall also indicate the quantity of food grains, drinking water, and medicines available in the shelter.

7.  The nodal officers shall verify the list of evacuees with the village-wise evacuation list already circulated. Any discrepancy shall be reported immediately.

8.  The Shelter Incharges shall not allow any outsider to enter the shelter without the permission of the DEOC Control Room. This restriction shall remain in force until the shelters are officially closed.

9.  The District Supply Officer shall ensure that the ration for the shelters is delivered on time. In case of any delay, the matter shall be reported to the DEOC Control Room.

10. The Block Development Officers shall make arrangements for the repair of approach roads to the shelters, if required, so that the evacuees can return to their villages without difficulty.

District Collector, Puri

Order No. DEOC/PURI/EVAC/2026/128
Date & Time: 15-07-2026, 14:30 Hrs.

Subject: Post-Landfall Directive – Shelter Management and Repatriation of Evacuees

The cyclone has made landfall and the wind speed has reduced considerably. However, the danger is not yet over. Heavy rain continues in several blocks and waterlogging is reported from low-lying areas. All Shelter Incharges and nodal officers shall continue to function until further orders. The following directions are issued for the management of shelters and the safe return of evacuees.

1.  No evacuee shall be permitted to leave the shelter until the DEOC issues an explicit "All Clear" message. The All Clear shall be communicated through the DEOC Control Room only, and not by any other authority. Shelters shall not act on verbal instructions or on the basis of weather reports received directly.

2.  Shelter Incharges shall prepare a list of evacuees shelter-wise, block-wise, and village-wise. The list shall show the number of families and persons still present in the shelter as on 15-07-2026 evening, and the number of families who have already returned to their villages on their own. This list shall be submitted to the DEOC Control Room by 20:00 Hrs. today.

3.  The transport arrangements made for evacuation shall be used in the reverse direction for repatriation. The vehicles shall be deployed only after the All Clear is given. The Shelter Incharge shall coordinate with the transport nodal officer for this purpose.

4.  The Shelter Incharges shall ensure that the shelters are cleaned before the evacuees are sent back. Drinking water and food arrangements shall continue until the last evacuee leaves the shelter. The health teams shall visit each shelter at least twice a day and report any case of illness to the DEOC Control Room.

5.  The DEOC Control Room shall maintain a register of all complaints received from evacuees regarding missing persons, lost belongings, or damage to houses. The register shall be handed over to the Revenue Department after the shelters are closed.

6.  The Shelter Incharges shall submit a daily report on the condition of the shelter building, including any damage to the roof, walls, or sanitary facilities. The report shall also indicate the quantity of food grains, drinking water, and medicines available in the shelter.

7.  The nodal officers shall verify the list of evacuees with the village-wise evacuation list already circulated. Any discrepancy shall be reported immediately.

8.  The Shelter Incharges shall not allow any outsider to enter the shelter without the permission of the DEOC Control Room. This restriction shall remain in force until the shelters are officially closed.

9.  The District Supply Officer shall ensure that the ration for the shelters is delivered on time. In case of any delay, the matter shall be reported to the DEOC Control Room.

10. The Block Development Officers shall make arrangements for the repair of approach roads to the shelters, if required, so that the evacuees can return to their villages without difficulty.

Sd/-
District Collector, Puri
